niche: Mind Hacks, AI Secrets, Bizarre Body Science & Hidden Power Dynamics

ideas.title: The Gas Pump Speed Trap Stealing Your Money
ideas.angle: Exposes why squeezing the gas pump handle to full speed vaporizes your fuel into invisible fumes that return to the underground tank while still charging your card. Ends with a challenge telling viewers to pump on the lowest click next time and comment their mileage difference.

hook.en: Stop pumping gas at full speed.

ideas.reason: Inflation and gas prices remain top-of-mind pain points globally; retail fuel mechanics and vapor recovery loops trigger immense curiosity and heated comment debate between drivers and mechanics.
sources: Petroleum Equipment Institute (PEI) fuel delivery standards
EPA Stage II Vapor Recovery Systems technical documentation

ideas.title: The Invariant Right Store Trap That Empties Your Wallet
ideas.angle: Reveals the architectural 'decompression zone' and the 'Invariant Right' reflex where 90% of shoppers subconsciously turn right upon entering a store, leading directly to the highest-margin impulse products. Drives massive comment engagement by asking viewers to predict which way they naturally turn in their local store.

hook.en: You always turn right entering stores.

ideas.reason: Retail dark architecture videos consistently hit 85%+ retention due to instant personal relatability; viewers realize their physical walking patterns have been pre-programmed by retail designers.
sources: Paco Underhill, Why We Buy: The Science of Shopping
Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services on shopper flow dynamics

ideas.title: The Decoy Effect Trap Hiding on Your Screen
ideas.angle: Breaks down how streaming services and SaaS platforms create an intentionally terrible tier just to manipulate 80% of users into choosing the expensive tier they never planned to buy. Challenges the viewer to look at their subscriptions right now and drop the one they were tricked into in the comments.

hook.en: Delete this subscription tier right now.

ideas.reason: Subscription fatigue is at an all-time high, making psychological breakdowns of SaaS and streaming pricing tiers instantly viral and highly shareable across social platforms.
sources: Dan Ariely, Predictably Irrational (The Economist subscription study)
Harvard Business Review on asymmetric dominance and consumer decision making
